paper.title: Revealing graph bandits for maximizing local influence

unmapped: Arms are the d nodes of an unknown graph (K = d); reward of node k is |S_{k,t}|, a sum of d independent Bernoulli(p_{k,j}) variables, so rewards are integers in [0,d] with variance at most r_k
settings.definition_quote: The restriction is that the learner, at round $t$, does not observe the set of influenced nodes $S_{k_t,t}$, but only the number number of elements in $S_{k_t,t}$, denoted by $\left|S_{k_t,t}\right|$.

settings.name_in_paper: Unrestricted local influence setting (revealing graph bandit)
unmapped: Arms are the d nodes of an unknown graph with influence matrix M=(p_{i,j}); reward is |S_{k_t,t}| (number of influenced nodes)
Beyond the reward, the learner observes the identity of the stochastic set S_{k_t,t} of influenced nodes (local edges revealed), which informs dual influences r_k^o
The graph is entirely unknown to the learner; d may exceed n
settings.definition_quote: At each round (time) $t$, the learner chooses a node $k_t$ and observes which nodes are influenced by $k_t$, i.e., the set $S_{k_t,t}$ of influenced nodes is \emph{revealed}. ... Given a budget of  $n$ rounds, the objective is to maximize the number of \emph{influences} that the selected node exerts.

bound.regime: n large enough depending on epsilon

conditions: eps*d < r_star < (1-eps)*d for some fixed eps>0
K = d nodes; mu_star = r_star (max expected influence)

source.label: thls
source.quote: Lower bound. If for some fixed $\varepsilon >0$, we have $\varepsilon d < r_\star < (1-\varepsilon)d$, then there exists a constant $\upsilon >0$ such that for $n$ large enough, depending on $\varepsilon$, we have that \[\inf\sup\EE{R_n} \geq \upsilon \min\left( r_\star n, r_\star d+\sqrt{r_{\star}nd}\right),\]

results.notes: Regret defined as n r_star - E[L_n], i.e. pseudo-regret. Theorem 4 in appendix restates this.

source.label: thls
source.quote: Upper bound.  There exists a constant $U>0$ such that the regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:2} is bounded as \[\EE {R_n} \leq U \min\left( r_\star n, r_\star d + \sqrt{r_{\star}nd}\right).\]

results.notes: Proof only sketched (follows MOSS analysis with Bernstein confidence).

symbols.D_star: detectable dimension D(Delta_star): number of nodes whose dual influence is within the detectable gap of the maximal dual influence
symbols.eps_star: influential-influenced gap: r_star minus max influence among most influenced nodes

tuning: bandit phase uses a minimax-optimal bandit algorithm such as GraphMOSS

source.label: BARE
source.quote: In the unrestricted local influence setting with information about the neighbors, \BARE satisfies, for a constant $C>0$, \[\EE{R_n} \leq C\min\left(r_\star n, D_\star r_{\star} + \sqrt{r_{\star}nD_\star} + n \varepsilon_\star\right).\]

conditions: undirected social network model (symmetric M, so eps_star = 0)

source.quote: For an undirected social network model the  expected regret of \BARE is \[\EE{R_n} \leq C\min\left(r_\star n, D_\star r_{\star} + \sqrt{r_{\star}nD_\star}\right),\] which is the minimax-optimal regret in the case where there are $D_\star$ instead of $d$ nodes.

results.notes: Special case of Theorem 2 with eps_star = 0.

symbols.r: bound on maximal influence of the problem class
symbols.D_bar: upper bound on detectable dimension D_star over the class
symbols.eps_bar: upper bound on influential-influenced gap over the class

conditions: d >= C n for a universal constant C
u*D_bar < r < (1-u)*D_bar for some fixed u>0
eps_bar <= u*sqrt(d*r/n) for small u if d <= n

source.label: BARE2
source.quote: Let $d \geq Cn>0$, where $C>0$ is a universal constant. Consider the set of unrestricted settings and the set of all problems that have maximal influence bounded by $r$ (where for some fixed $u >0$, we have $u \overline D < r < (1-u)\overline D$), $D_\star \leq \overline D$ and influential-influence gap smaller than $\varepsilon$ ... Then the expected regret of the best possible algorithm in the worst case of these problems is lower bounded as \[C''\min\left(rn,  \overline Dr + \sqrt{rn\overline D}  + n \varepsilon\right),\]

results.notes: Minimax over the class of problems with parameters r, D_bar, eps_bar. Restated as Theorem 5 in appendix. Condition d >= Cn conflicts somewhat with the 'if d <= n' clause; recorded as stated.
